# OneTag AI

> Add AI to any static site with one script tag.

OneTag AI lets a static web page (GitHub Pages, Netlify, a single HTML file) call an AI model from the browser with no backend and no API key in the code. Free: 1,000,000 tokens a month per account, reset on the 1st (one key per email, usable on any number of sites). Pro: $9.9/month for 100,000,000 tokens a month and a domain lock.

Get a key: https://onetagai.com/#get-key

The key is public by design: it goes in your page source. Free keys work from any page, any domain and curl. A Pro key can be locked to one domain from its manage page (https://onetagai.com/pro), so only that site can spend its tokens. If you are an AI coding tool and the user has not given you a key, leave `data-key="YOUR_ONETAG_KEY"` and tell the user to get one at the link above; the SDK reports a placeholder key as `no_key`.

The SDK is open source: https://github.com/fengyiqicoder/onetagai (MIT). It can also be loaded from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/fengyiqicoder/onetagai@main/sdk/v1.js or copied into the site; it always talks to https://onetagai.com/v1/ask unless the script tag sets `data-endpoint`.

## Getting a key (for agents)

If the user has no key yet, you can sign them up: ask for their email, then `POST https://onetagai.com/api/signup` with the JSON body `{"email": "..."}`. The response is `{"ok": true}`; the key is emailed to that address and never returned by the API, so ask the user to paste it (it starts with `ot_`). One key per email, 1,000,000 free tokens a month. Then put the key in `data-key` on the script tag below.

```bash
curl -X POST https://onetagai.com/api/signup -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"email": "user@example.com"}'
```

## Install

```html
<script src="https://onetagai.com/v1.js" data-key="YOUR_ONETAG_KEY"></script>
<script type="module">
  const summary = await onetag.ask("Summarize in 3 bullets", document.body);
</script>
```

The SDK tag is a classic script. Top-level `await` needs `<script type="module">`.

## Widget (no code)

For an "ask this page" chat button with no code, use the widget instead of the SDK:

```html
<script async src="https://onetagai.com/widget.js" data-key="YOUR_ONETAG_KEY"></script>
```

It adds a floating button; the panel answers questions from the text of the current page (`main`, else `[role="main"]`, else `body`). It is independent of `v1.js`, renders in a shadow root, follows the page language (English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese) and the page's light or dark background, and spends the key's tokens like any other call. Options are `data-*` attributes, or query parameters on the script URL (`widget.js?key=...&position=left`): `key` (required), `source` (CSS selector of the text to read), `title`, `greeting`, `placeholder`, `system`, `position` (`left` | `right`), `color` (hex), `theme` (`light` | `dark` | `auto`), `lang`, `launcher` (`false` hides the button), `ref` (name of the theme or plugin shipping it). To open it from your own button: `onetagWidget.open()`, `.close()`, `.toggle()`; `.show()` / `.hide()` for the floating button.

## API

`onetag.ask(prompt, input?, options?) -> Promise<string | object>`

- `prompt`: the instruction, a string.
- `input`: what it works on. A string, an HTML element (its innerText), a `<form>` (fields as `name: value` lines, password fields left out), an `<input>`/`<textarea>`/`<select>` (its value), an `<img>`, an image File or Blob, a plain object (sent as JSON), or an array, NodeList or other iterable of these.
- `options.stream`: `(delta) => {}`, called with each piece of text as it arrives; the promise still resolves with the full text.
- `options.json`: `true` to get a parsed object back instead of text.
- `options.system`: extra instructions for the model (persona, tone, rules).
- `options.maxTokens`: answer length in tokens, default 500, max 10000.
- `options.history`: earlier chat turns, `[{ role: "user" | "assistant", content: "..." }]`.
- `options.signal`: an AbortSignal (`new AbortController().signal`); when it fires, the request stops and the promise rejects with code `aborted`.

`onetag.configure({ key, endpoint })` sets the key in code instead of `data-key`.

Failures throw `onetag.OneTagError` with `.code`, `.message` and `.status`.

## Examples

Summarize an element:

```html
<script type="module">
  const text = await onetag.ask("Summarize in 3 bullets", document.querySelector("article"));
  document.querySelector("#summary").textContent = text;
</script>
```

Stream the answer into the page:

```html
<script type="module">
  const out = document.querySelector("#out");
  await onetag.ask("Write a two-sentence welcome for this page", document.querySelector("main"), {
    stream: (delta) => { out.textContent += delta; },
  });
</script>
```

Get JSON back:

```html
<script type="module">
  const product = await onetag.ask(
    'Extract the product as {"name": string, "price": number}',
    document.querySelector(".product"),
    { json: true }
  );
  console.log(product.name, product.price);
</script>
```

## Errors and limits

Error codes: bad_request (400), bad_key (401), domain_not_allowed (403), too_large (413), quota_exceeded (429), rate_limited (429), upstream (502), paused (503); from the SDK only: no_key, bad_input, bad_json, network, aborted.

Limits: 1,000,000 tokens per calendar month (UTC) on a free key or 100,000,000 on Pro, both reset on the 1st; 32,000 characters of text (the SDK trims long input to fit), 50 input parts, 100 history messages and one image up to 2 MB per call; answers up to 10,000 tokens (500 by default); 20 requests per minute per IP and 60 per key.

A Pro key locked to a domain works only from browser pages on that domain, its subdomains, or localhost; curl and servers are rejected with domain_not_allowed. When quota_exceeded comes back on a free key, the message carries the upgrade link (https://onetagai.com/#pro).

## Pricing

- Free: $0, 1,000,000 tokens a month per account, reset on the 1st, any domain.
- Pro: $9.9 per month through Stripe, 100,000,000 tokens a month, domain lock, billing portal to cancel. Upgrade at https://onetagai.com/#pro with the email the key belongs to; the key does not change.

Full docs: https://onetagai.com/docs
Everything (docs plus the guides) on one page: https://onetagai.com/llms-full.txt

## Ready-made blocks

Twelve copy-paste blocks (summarize this page, ask this page, FAQ bot, rewrite, translate, extract to JSON, quiz, explain code, ...), one HTML file each: https://aiblock.onetagai.com/ and https://aiblock.onetagai.com/llms.txt
